claims.value: Diplomatic relations with the United States

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.note: The official history dates diplomatic relations to 1862 and states that strong ties continued into the 1990s; this record is restricted to the atlas framework.

qualifications: Diplomatic relationship, not United States sovereignty over Liberia.
No assertion of identical diplomatic staffing, financial support or agreement throughout the interval.
Coarse research endpoint years remain partial; earlier or later events are not back-projected.

claims.value: An international commission submitted its report on slavery and forced labour to the Liberian government.

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.note: The contemporary memorandum explicitly dates submission to 8 September 1930.

qualifications: The commission included American, League of Nations-nominated and Liberian members. Findings are attributed to the commission; submission is not evidence that the abuses immediately ceased.

claims.value: The Liberian president notified the United States that the government accepted the international commission’s recommendations.

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.note: The memorandum records the notification on 30 September and distinguishes promises from implemented reforms.

qualifications: The same memorandum reports that definite implementation plans had not yet been received. Acceptance must not be represented as completed abolition or implementation.

claims.value: Sokoto; Gwandu for the western emirates

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.locator: Twin capital at Gwandu; eastern and western emirates; capital district Sokoto
evidence.note: The country study describes the principal caliph at Sokoto and the western administrative capital at Gwandu. This conservative late-century interval precedes British conquest and does not substitute modern Nigerian capitals.

qualifications: Sokoto retained primacy; Gwandu administered the western division. The centres are not flattened into identical roles.
No territorial geometry or statistical scope is inferred.

claims.value: Usman dan Fodio — Islamic scholar and reformer associated with the founding of the Sokoto caliphate

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.locator: Radical mallams; jihad beginning in Gobir in 1804; broad religious and political impact
evidence.note: The country study establishes his religious reform movement and historical influence, independently of routine officeholding. The Library of Congress identifies him as the author of a surviving religious manuscript and dates his lifespan.

evidence.locator: Title, Names, Summary and Rights & Access metadata
evidence.note: Catalogue identifies Usuman dan Fodio (1754–1817) as author of a work concerning the authority of Islamic scholars. The broad catalogue publication range is not a dated publication event.

qualifications: His significance rests on religious scholarship, reform and documented broad influence, not merely officeholding.
The manuscript catalogue does not establish a precise composition date; no work is asserted to have appeared by 1815 solely from its catalogue date range.
No disputed date of transfer of administrative power to Muhammad Bello is resolved here.

figure.name: Usman dan Fodio
figure.relationship: Scholar and reformer whose movement founded the Sokoto caliphate; not a back-projected modern Nigerian nationality.
figure.activity: Living founder and religious intellectual relevant to the caliphate in 1815; no assertion of a particular newly published work in that year.
figure.contribution: Islamic reformist scholarship and a movement with major political and religious consequences across the savanna and Sahel.

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.locator: Pages 1–2 and 11: Bolama first capital; Bissau capital transfer in 1941
evidence.note: The archival account dates separation from Cape Verde to 18 March 1879 and identifies Bolama as the first capital until the 1941 transfer. Only the existing colony framework is covered.

qualifications: Not the modern Guinea-Bissau capital projected backwards. Capital transition year 1941 is retained at year precision; 1880 remains a partial editorial boundary under scanner policy.

claims.value: Portuguese colonial military campaigns led by João Teixeira Pinto began in March 1913 and continued into July 1915.

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.locator: Page 2: campaigns from March 1913 to July 1915
evidence.note: The archival history gives the campaign interval; the event record stores its actual starting month and explicitly preserves the subsequent duration.

qualifications: Selected 1914 snapshot receives dated 1913 context under existing rules; the start is not relabelled as 1914.
Military campaigns against local communities do not establish that the whole mapped colony had uniform effective sovereignty.
